instructions:
# Role

You are the reasoning component of an AI Engineering Agent. You do not draw CAD and you do not
compute checks yourself: Python performs calculations, rule checks and registration, and Fusion 360
builds and measures geometry. Your job is engineering judgement: interpret, identify gaps, state
assumptions, plan, and decide on revisions.

Rules that always apply:
- Answer with ONE JSON object that validates against the response schema. No prose outside it.
- Never invent requirements, regulations or rule values. Only rules listed in the context exist.
- Never claim FIA compliance, structural safety, race-readiness or production readiness.
- Do not silently invent critical information. Anything not stated by the user is either a
  missing-information item (ASK) or an explicit assumption (A-id) - never a hidden default.
- Every numeric design value must trace to requirement ids (R..), assumption ids (A..),
  user answers (M..) or rule ids. Units: mm, deg, N, kg.
- Be concise and specific; write for an engineer reviewing your reasoning later.


# Task: design review after CAD + validation

context.validation lists every check result (status, severity, measured, limit, message).
context.blocking_failures lists the results that prevent acceptance.

Decide:
- ACCEPT  - only if there are no blocking failures (Python enforces this) and the result meets the
            requirements. Advisory findings may remain; mention them in the rationale.
- REVISE  - give `parameter_changes` (only changed parameters, full PlannedParam entries) that fix
            the findings. Python re-checks and rebuilds. Revision loops are limited (context.loops).
- STOP    - the request cannot be met with this generator/inputs; explain why.

Do not accept a design to "finish the task". An honest STOP is better than an unjustified ACCEPT.

context.request: Design a machined aluminium L-bracket to mount a 2 kg sensor box to a flat plate with four M6 bolts.

steps: Fix the interfaces first: base leg = 2x2 M6 pattern for the plate (R03, A05); upright = 1x2 M5 pattern 40 mm apart (R07/M01).
Size clearance holes from ISO 273 medium series (STD-ISO273-MEDIUM): M6 -> 6.6 mm, M5 -> 5.5 mm.
Set width and hole positions so every hole centre is >= 1.5 d from free edges (GL-HOLE-EDGE-DISTANCE) and clear of the bend fillet.
Choose plate thickness from the bending hand calculation (A03 load, A02 material) with margin for bolt clamping; respect min wall 2 mm (DFM-MACH-WALL-MIN).
Internal bend radius >= 3 mm for end-mill access (DFM-MACH-INNER-RADIUS-MIN) and >= 0.2 t (DFM-DFMEA-FATIGUE-FILLET).
Build the parametric model in Fusion (named user parameters, constrained sketches, named features).
Inspect read-only in Fusion; verify body count, feature health, bounding box, volume, parameters and every interface hole.
Review results; revise parameters if any blocking check fails.

bracket_thickness.rationale: Hand calc at 4 mm already gives SF ~9 on yield; 5 mm chosen for bolt-clamping stiffness and thread-free clearance holes; > 2 mm min wall.

bend_inner_radius.rationale: >= 3 mm end-mill radius rule and >= 0.2 t = 1 mm fatigue rule; 4 mm leaves margin for an 8 mm cutter.

bracket_width.rationale: M5 pitch 40 mm + 2 x 1.5 x 5.5 mm edge distance = 56.5 mm min -> 60 mm.

leg_base_length.rationale: Last base hole row at 52 mm + 1.5 x 6.6 = 61.9 mm min -> 64 mm.

leg_upright_height.rationale: Hole row at 35 mm + 1.5 x 5.5 mm = 43.3 mm min; 50 mm gives a flat mounting face around the holes.

base_hole_x0.rationale: 17 mm from the upright inner face for M6 hex head / socket access (A07); clear of the 9 mm bend zone.

base_hole_pitch_x.rationale: Spread the 4 bolts along the leg to resist the overturning moment.

base_hole_pitch_y.rationale: Side edge distance (60/2 - 18) = 12 mm = 1.82 d >= 1.5 d.

base_hole_rows.rationale: Four M6 bolts as a 2 x 2 pattern.

base_hole_cols.rationale: Four M6 bolts as a 2 x 2 pattern.

upright_hole_z0.rationale: Hole row 35 mm above the plate keeps the sensor box clear of the base leg and bend (A06).

upright_hole_pitch_y.rationale: Sensor box M5 holes 40 mm apart (user answer).

upright_hole_rows.rationale: Two bolts side by side = one row.

load_case.description: 2 kg sensor box x 5 g, applied at its centre of mass 40 mm from the upright face: constant bending moment on the upright.

new_assumptions.text: The sensor box can be mounted with its M5 hole row 35 mm above the plate (box bottom clears the base leg and bend).
new_assumptions.rationale: Box dimensions unknown; 35 mm keeps the box above the 9 mm bend zone.
new_assumptions.impact: If the box hole row must be lower, upright_hole_z0 can be reduced to >= 11.75 mm.

new_assumptions.text: M6 hex-head bolts with washers, installed from above with a socket: >= 15 mm clearance from hole centre to the upright inner face.
new_assumptions.rationale: Tool access for the base bolts next to the upright.

verification_plan: Pre-CAD (Python): ISO 273 clearance holes, wall thickness, internal radius, fatigue radius ratio, hole edge distance, bending hand calc.
Fusion (read-only inspection): one solid body, all features healthy, sketches fully constrained, bbox 64 x 60 x 50 mm, volume vs analytic model, user parameters = record.
Interfaces: all 4 base and 2 upright holes located in Fusion geometry at designed position, axis and diameter.

assumptions.text: Concept-level design: nominal geometry, no tolerancing, no FEA/fatigue analysis; sizing by hand calculation only.
assumptions.impact: Results are not a structural sign-off.

assumptions.rationale: Most common general-purpose machining alloy; user said 'aluminium' only.
assumptions.impact: Yield strength 276 MPa (handbook, not verified) used in the bending check.

assumptions.text: Design load = 2 kg x 5 g = 98.1 N applied at the box centre of mass, 40 mm from the upright face (R08), i.e. bending moment 3924 N*mm on the upright; required safety factor on yield 2.0.
assumptions.rationale: No environment given; 5 g covers handling, shock and vibration typical of vehicle-mounted equipment at concept level.
assumptions.impact: Drives plate thickness; must be confirmed for the real environment.

assumptions.text: No hard envelope limit; keep the bracket compact (each leg < 100 mm, width <= 70 mm).
assumptions.impact: Leg lengths/width chosen from hole layout and edge-distance rules only.

assumptions.text: The flat plate will be drilled to match the bracket; base holes in a 2 x 2 rectangular pattern with ISO 273 medium clearance (6.6 mm).
assumptions.impact: Base hole pattern is defined by the bracket and must be transferred to the plate.

assumptions.text: The sensor box can be mounted with its M5 hole row 35 mm above the plate (box bottom clears the base leg and bend).
assumptions.rationale: Box dimensions unknown; 35 mm keeps the box above the 9 mm bend zone.
assumptions.impact: If the box hole row must be lower, upright_hole_z0 can be reduced to >= 11.75 mm.

assumptions.text: M6 hex-head bolts with washers, installed from above with a socket: >= 15 mm clearance from hole centre to the upright inner face.
assumptions.rationale: Tool access for the base bolts next to the upright.
